full_judgment: 2. One Jadav Chandra Mali who has since died, filed an application under section 96 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act (hereinafter referred to) as "The State Acquisition Act") for pre-emption of certain lands which appertained to a holding recorded in Khatian No. 55 of Mouza Shahadebpur. The pre-emptor claimed that the said holding was owned by him and the respondents No. 2 to 5 and that the respondent No.1, who was a stranger, purchased 13 acre of land thereof from respondents No. 2 and 3 by a kabala dated 3-2-1964 without service of any notice upon him. According to the pre-emptor he came to know about the sale for the first time in Falgoon, 1371 B.S. when a temporary but was raised on the land. The purchaser resisted the claim for pre-emption on the ground that the pre-emptor had knowledge of the purchase and that the disputed land was a Chandina land within a Municipal area and therefore section 96 of the State Acquisition Act had no application to the purchase in question. The learned Munsif allowed the application for pre-emption and his decision was affirmed on appeal by a Subordinate Judge. The respondent No.1, the purchaser, thereupon filed an application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure in the High Court. In the High Court a petition was filed on behalf of the pre-emptor under Order 6, rule 17 read with section 151 and Section 153 of the Code of Civil Procedure for amendment of the application for pre-emption whereby the application for pre-emption was sought to be converted to an application under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act but the application was rejected on the ground that it would change the nature of the case. The learned Judges came to the finding that as the land in question was within a Municipal area, section 96 of the State Acquisition Act was wrongly applied by the Courts below and upon this finding made the rule obtained by the respondent No. 1 absolute and set aside the order of the learned Subordinate Judge.
